correctness.rationale: Let N=8n+1. Since tau(N)=product(e_p+1), v_2(tau(N))<=1 implies either every exponent even, hence odd square N=(2m+1)^2 and n=T_m, or precisely one odd exponent, e_p≡1 mod4, and N=p^(4a+1)v². Modulo 8 forces p≡1 mod8. Quadratic reciprocity (2/p)=1 and the Euclidean norm property of Z[sqrt2] (nearest integer error norm <1) show p splits as p=A²−2C², with C even by mod8, hence p=A²−8B². Scaling by p^(2a)v yields N=X²−8Y² with odd X and desired n=T_m−Y²; signs normalized. Own factor/exponent checks for n<3000 and explicit small norm-prime witnesses corroborate both branches; no finite check used to prove all n.
